# Incident Report — MTA 2024-07-30 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim host
| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 172.16.1.66 | Consistent source across all identity artifacts below |
| MAC | 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08 | ARP: `172.16.1.66 → 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08` |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-SKBR25F | NBNS: `172.16.1.66 DESKTOP-SKBR25F<00>/<20>`; also self-reported inside the C2 beacon (below) |
| Logged-in user | ccollier | Kerberos `CNameString` for AS-REQ/TGS-REQ traffic from 172.16.1.66 to DC 172.16.1.4; also self-reported inside the C2 beacon |

Domain controller for context: 172.16.1.4 (WIRESHARK-WS-DC, domain `wiresharkworkshop.online`), reached via normal LDAP/Kerberos/DCERPC traffic — not implicated in the intrusion.

## Malware family
**STRRAT** (Java-based RAT/backdoor, known for browser-credential theft and fake-ransomware extension behavior).

**Attribution: signature-confirmed.** The infected host's outbound TCP stream 83 (172.16.1.66:49754 → 141.98.10.79:12132) carries a literal, unencrypted pipe-delimited beacon that self-identifies the malware by name:

```
ping|STRRAT|1BE8292C|DESKTOP-SKBR25F|ccollier|Microsoft Windows 11 Pro|64-bit|Windows Defender|<base64>|1.6|US:United States|Not Installed|<uptime>
```

Fields decode to: protocol tag `ping`, malware family `STRRAT`, campaign/bot ID `1BE8292C`, victim hostname, victim username, OS (Windows 11 Pro, 64-bit), installed AV (Windows Defender), a base64-encoded active-window title (values seen: `SG9tZQ==`→"Home", `UHJvZ3JhbSBNYW5hZ2Vy`→"Program Manager"), client version `1.6`, geo `US:United States`, firewall status `Not Installed`, and system idle time. This is the documented STRRAT check-in format, not an inference — the string names the family directly.

## C2 behavior
- The host beacons to **141.98.10.79:12132** every ~5 seconds for the full duration of the capture (first beacon at t=76.99s, last at t≈585.66s — over 8 minutes of continuous check-ins).
- The channel is **plaintext TCP on a non-standard port (12132)** with no TLS handshake — consistent with STRRAT's known unencrypted C2 protocol.
- No DNS lookup for 141.98.10.79 appears anywhere in the capture — the malware connects by hardcoded IP, not domain, so there is no C2 domain to report.
- No file transfer, jar payload, or additional attacker command (beyond the repeating `ping` beacon) was observed within the capture window; only `--export-objects http` output present is benign (`www.msftconnecttest.com/connecttest.txt`, `ip-api.com/json/`). Delivery of the initial STRRAT jar itself is **not captured** in this PCAP (occurred before capture start or via a channel not present here).

## Indicators of Compromise (grounded in this capture only)

| Type | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| C2 endpoint | **141.98.10.79:12132** | tcp.stream 83, 172.16.1.66:49754 ↔ 141.98.10.79:12132, plaintext STRRAT `ping` beacons, ~5s interval, ~11526 packets/session |
| Malware family marker | `STRRAT` string, bot ID `1BE8292C`, version `1.6` | Literal field values inside every beacon on stream 83 |
| Domain | none observed | C2 reached by raw IP; no DNS query for 141.98.10.79 exists in the capture |
| URL | none observed | No HTTP request in the capture points at attacker infrastructure |
| File name / SHA256 | none observed | No payload transfer captured; only benign objects (`connecttest.txt`, ip-api JSON) were exported |

## Benign context (noise, not IOCs)
Standard Windows/Office/Edge telemetry and connectivity checks to Microsoft-owned infrastructure: `www.msftconnecttest.com`, `login.microsoftonline.com`, `*.events.data.microsoft.com`, `*.msn.com`, `officeclient.microsoft.com`, `odc.officeapps.live.com`, `client.wns.windows.com`, `config.edge.skype.com`, `ecs.office.com`, `g.live.com`, `go.microsoft.com`, Bing/MSN CDN hosts, plus domain traffic (LDAP/Kerberos/CLDAP/NBNS/DCERPC) to DC 172.16.1.4. Also benign: `github.com`/`objects.githubusercontent.com`, `repo1.maven.org`, `javadl-esd-secure.oracle.com` (Java runtime present/updating — consistent with a Java-based RAT needing a JRE, but the fetches themselves are legitimate vendor traffic). The single Chrome-UA request to `ip-api.com/json/` (frame 9111) returned a normal geolocation JSON and is not by itself malicious traffic, though such lookups are commonly performed by loaders/RATs for victim fingerprinting; it is not tied to the STRRAT beacon by protocol or evidence and is listed here rather than as a confirmed IOC.

## Incident summary
The Windows 11 workstation DESKTOP-SKBR25F (172.16.1.66, MAC 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08), logged in as user **ccollier**, is infected with the **STRRAT** Java RAT (bot ID 1BE8292C, client v1.6). Starting at t≈77s and continuing through the end of the capture, the malware beacons in plaintext every ~5 seconds to its C2 at **141.98.10.79:12132**, self-reporting hostname, username, OS, and AV status. The infection vector and any payload/credential exfiltration are not visible within this capture — only the ongoing check-in beacon is present.
